workarounds.what: The display holds one worker source per URL only while a layer reads it, and its proxies look that source up at each render, because the engine's CogTilerEngine._assetSources keeps a mosaic's asset proxies by URL until destroy() and reuses them.

pin_test.title: pin: the engine reuses a mosaic's cached asset proxy after the layer left, and that proxy still draws

workarounds.exit: The engine evicts a mosaic's asset proxies with its layer or gives a release hook (opengeos/maplibre-gl-raster#79); the pin then fails and displaySources can hold one handle per proxy again.

workarounds.what: The pool client stands in for the cog-tiler module through LayerManager's loadCogTiler dependency, cast once with `deps as never` because the published declaration types it through a symbol the pinned cog-tiler-wasm does not export.
workarounds.exit: The loadCogTiler dependency is typed as a public interface a custom client satisfies; the cast goes.

workarounds.what: The pool owns tile scheduling (newest first, a bounded number per lane, a tile that left the viewport rejected before it starts) because the engine never forwards MapLibre's abort signal to the cog-tiler render call.
workarounds.exit: The engine forwards each tile request's AbortSignal to the render call; the pool's relevance filter can then defer to it.

workarounds.what: Until every desired layer reaches the map, the display re-applies on idle and sourcedata once the style reports loaded, because the engine gates its first mutation on isStyleLoaded() and then waits for a style event a settled style never emits.
workarounds.exit: A layer added while the basemap still loads reaches the map with no later styledata; the nudge goes.

workarounds.what: Map errors reach the raster display by matching the engine's private source id prefix (/^mlrcog\d+-/).
workarounds.exit: The engine exposes a stable id scheme or an ownsSource(id) query, or Phase 2d's ownsResource routes errors without the prefix; both matches go.

workarounds.what: Only cog-tiler's reads run in the pool's lanes: the deps supply no loadGeoTIFF, so the engine still reads each layer's COG header (band count, names, palette) on the UI thread through its own.
workarounds.exit: The engine reads headers through the cog-tiler dependency or a worker-capable loadGeoTIFF, so every read runs in a lane.

workarounds.what: Each lane replaces an opened source's private tileCache map, capped by entry count only, with a BudgetedTileCache charged to one lane-wide byte budget, and open fails loudly if the field is gone.
workarounds.exit: cog-tiler accepts a byte budget or a pluggable decoded-block cache; the swap goes.

workarounds.what: Past a display COG's native zoom the lane draws each tile from its native ancestor with a one-pixel halo, upsampled at output pixel centres, because cog-tiler samples output pixels at their corners and picks overview levels by float comparison, which draws seams.

pin_test.title: [expected-fail upstream cog-tiler-wasm corner sampling, canopi-xgvh] adjacent derivatives and an item under them meet with no gap, step or under-line

workarounds.exit: A cog-tiler-wasm release that samples at (px + 0.5) / outW, reads its window with a halo and chooses levels without float ties: the pin's it.fails then fails, overzoom.ts and raster-display-overzoom.test.ts are deleted and the marker is lifted in one change.

workarounds.what: Linux startup sets WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1 before Tauri starts WebKit, because WebKitGTK's DMA-BUF renderer can deadlock WebGL context creation and MapLibre needs WebGL.
workarounds.exit: A WebKitGTK release Tauri ships with creates WebGL contexts under the DMA-BUF renderer; re-tested on each WebKitGTK or Tauri bump, the variable goes.

workarounds.what: The CRS authority uses proj4rs, pinned =0.2.0 as the reference points measure it, instead of wbprojection, which placed national grids 30 m to 1,262 km off (canopi-ji73).
workarounds.exit: A wbprojection release places the reference points (EPSG 28992, 31370, 27700, 31287, 2100, 2169, 5514, 2263) within proj4rs's tolerance, or Canopi keeps proj4rs and closes this row.

workarounds.what: desktop/Cargo.toml takes wbgeotiff from a whitebox-wasm git revision, as no crates.io release publishes it.
workarounds.report: declined 2026-09-27: the user declined posting upstream issues for whitebox-wasm (canopi-2d1b)
workarounds.exit: wbgeotiff is published as a release; the dependency moves to it.

workarounds.what: Each windowed GeoLibre tool run gets RAYON_NUM_THREADS=2 and heavy jobs run one at a time, because the hydrology tools use all cores whatever RAYON_NUM_THREADS says.
workarounds.report: declined 2026-09-27: the user declined posting upstream issues for geolibre-rust (canopi-2d1b)
workarounds.exit: The tools respect RAYON_NUM_THREADS or a --threads flag; the one-heavy-job rule can then admit more.

workarounds.what: desktop/web/package.json overrides image-size (via @deck.gl/geo-layers and texture-compressor), fflate (via pdfkit and loaders.gl) and texture-compressor's argparse to ranges npm audit accepts.
workarounds.report: none: no upstream bug; each parent's own range is safe in a later release, which Renovate shows
workarounds.exit: Each parent's own range is safe; its override is removed.

workarounds.library: Tauri 2's Linux GTK3 stack (wry, webkit2gtk-rs, gtk3-rs) and the zbus 5 plugins (tauri-plugin-opener, tauri-plugin-single-instance)
workarounds.what: policy/advisories.json accepts RUSTSEC advisories Canopi cannot fix: glib 0.18's unsound VariantStrIter and the unmaintained proc-macro-error, from the GTK3 webview chain through tauri, muda and gtk 0.18, and the unmaintained zvariant, zbus_names and zvariant_derive, zbus 5 parts that tauri-plugin-opener and tauri-plugin-single-instance pull (not the GTK3 chain; 2.1-M313).
workarounds.report: none: Tauri's own move to GTK4 retires the chain; tracked only (2.1-M204)
workarounds.exit: Tauri on GTK4 (2.1-M204) and both plugins off zbus 5: OSV no longer reports these advisories, scripts/advisories.py check fails their entries as stale, and the bump removes them from policy/advisories.json and regenerates osv-scanner.toml.

workarounds.what: The Firefox projects run headed under Xvfb, one worker at a time, because headless Firefox in the pinned image creates no WebGL context (every driver option refused), so the map never draws there; headed Firefox gets Mesa's software WebGL 2.
workarounds.report: none: an environment limit of the pinned image's headless Firefox, re-tested on each Playwright bump
workarounds.exit: A Playwright image whose headless Firefox creates a WebGL context: the Firefox projects run headless and the Xvfb wrapper goes.

workarounds.what: In Firefox the map specs expect the whole console line 'Shared workspace map failed: Error' instead of the message prefix, because Playwright's Firefox gives an Error argument's console text as its name alone, without the message.

pin_test.title: Retry rebuilds exactly one map in the map container

workarounds.exit: A Playwright release whose Firefox console text carries the Error's message: the Firefox run of the pin then logs a line the spec does not expect and fails, and both specs expect the full prefix in every engine.
